descriptors.definition: The standard prescribes accounting principles for property, plant, and equipment to allow financial statement users to understand entity investments and changes therein. It applies universally unless another standard mandates alternative treatments or excludes specific assets like biological assets or mineral rights.
inclusion: Tangible items held for production, supply, rental, or administrative use expected to last over one period
PPE used to develop or maintain biological assets, exploration assets, and mineral reserves
exclusion: PPE classified as held for sale
Biological assets related to agricultural activity other than bearer plants
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from investment property by applying the cost model for owned investment property under specific guidance
Distinguished from biological assets by excluding non-bearer living plants

descriptors.definition: The standard governs all property, plant, and equipment accounting practices unless separate standards dictate unique methods. It specifies broad exclusions while maintaining coverage for assets supporting excluded extractive or agricultural operations.
inclusion: Tangible assets applied in administrative, supply, or production functions extending past one accounting period
exclusion: Assets governed exclusively by alternate standards such as Ind AS 105 or Ind AS 41
nearby_distinctions: Separates general operational infrastructure from specialized extractive and biological resource properties

descriptors.definition: This section outlines fundamental measurement terms governing asset valuation, residual allocations, and impairment tracking under the standard. It defines calculations for determining current book values against recoverable economic worth.
inclusion: Valuation definitions including fair value, carrying value, and recoverable limits
exclusion: General operational rules or recognition thresholds not tied directly to valuation terms
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes fair value market participant pricing from entity-specific internal cash flow estimations

descriptors.definition: Property, plant, and equipment costs qualify for asset recognition only when future economic benefits are probable and the item's cost can be reliably measured. Entities evaluate all initial acquisition expenses and subsequent operational expenditures using these core criteria.
inclusion: Initial asset acquisition costs meeting probability and measurement tests
Stand-by and servicing equipment meeting asset definitions
exclusion: Spare parts and servicing tools failing asset criteria which default to inventory classification
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes capitalized equipment spares from routine inventory spares based on operational deployment and holding period

descriptors.definition: An asset item is capitalized if and only if future economic inflows are probable and historical costs can be calculated reliably. This threshold dictates initial balance sheet inclusion for both foundational acquisitions and subsequent enhancement outlays.
inclusion: Costs satisfying both the probability of economic benefits and reliable measurement conditions
exclusion: Expenditures failing either probability or measurement thresholds
nearby_distinctions: Separates capitalizable outlays from standard period operational expenses

descriptors.concept_name: Recognition of Spare parts, stand-by equipment and servicing equipment
descriptors.definition: Specialized spare parts and stand-by equipment are categorized as property, plant, and equipment when they satisfy the standard asset definition. Items failing this threshold are treated as ordinary inventory supplies.
inclusion: Servicing and standby items utilized over multiple periods alongside primary assets
exclusion: Routine replacement parts classified under standard inventory rules
nearby_distinctions: Differentiates major capital spares from routine operational consumables stored for quick turnover

descriptors.concept_name: Unit of measurement for recognition of PPE and Aggregation of individually insignificant items
descriptors.definition: The standard does not mandate a universal recognition unit, requiring professional judgment to establish what constitutes an individual property item. Individually immaterial assets like tools and dies may be aggregated to apply recognition principles collectively.
inclusion: Aggregated minor tools, moulds, and dies evaluated collectively under materiality judgment
exclusion: Standalone major assets evaluated on an individual component basis
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes collective asset pools for minor tools from individually distinct heavy machinery items

descriptors.definition: Assets acquired for safety or environmental reasons qualify for recognition because they enable entities to extract future economic benefits from related assets. Without these compliance enhancements, underlying production assets could not legally or safely operate.
inclusion: Safety and environmental installations required to unlock operational benefits from other assets
exclusion: Discretionary outlays not tied to regulatory necessity or operational enablement
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes compliance-driven asset enhancements from direct revenue-generating machinery

descriptors.definition: Subsequent expenditures that replace parts of an asset or execute major overhauls are capitalized if recognition criteria are met, alongside the derecognition of old component carrying values. Conversely, routine day-to-day servicing costs are expensed immediately as incurred.
inclusion: Costs of scheduled component replacements and major overhauls meeting recognition tests
exclusion: Day-to-day servicing, minor repairs, and consumable labor costs
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes long-interval capital overhauls from routine day-to-day maintenance charges routed through profit or loss

descriptors.definition: Qualifying items of property, plant, and equipment are initially recorded at historical cost upon acquisition or construction. Cost components include purchase prices, directly attributable preparation outlays, and initial dismantling obligations.
inclusion: Purchase prices, site preparation, delivery, installation, and asset dismantling provisions
exclusion: General administrative overheads and abnormal waste expenses
nearby_distinctions: Separates initial acquisition cost models from subsequent revaluation or depreciation measurements

descriptors.definition: Property, plant, and equipment items eligible for asset recognition must be quantified initially at their total cost base. This base encapsulates net purchase pricing, direct setup outlays, and future site restoration obligations.
inclusion: Net purchase outlays, import duties, handling fees, and professional installation charges
exclusion: Refundable taxes, trade discounts, and general overhead costs
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes initial cost capitalisation from later fair value adjustments

descriptors.definition: The asset cost baseline comprises purchase considerations, direct bringing-to-location expenses, and estimated dismantling provisions. For self-constructed assets, internal manufacturing profits and abnormal material wastage are strictly excluded from the capitalized total.
inclusion: Direct labor, material, and site preparation costs for self-constructed assets
exclusion: Abnormal amounts of wasted material or labor and internal manufacturing profits
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes standard construction outlays from abnormal inefficiencies excluded from asset values
